summary: Now the mishnah lists people who get lashes. First are those who have a forbidden relationship with certain relatives, and Kohanim or others who marry someone the Torah does not allow them to marry.
stIntro: After enumerating in tractate Sanhedrin those liable to be executed and in the previous chapter those liable to be exiled, the mishna proceeds to enumerate those liable to receive lashes.

chunks.en: And these are the ones who get lashes:
chunks.st: These are the people who are flogged by Torah law for violating a prohibition:

chunks.en: one who has a forbidden relationship with his sister,
chunks.st: One who engages in intercourse with his sister,

chunks.en: or his father's sister,
chunks.st: or with his father’s sister,

chunks.en: or his mother's sister,
chunks.st: or with his mother’s sister,

chunks.en: or his wife's sister,
chunks.st: or with his wife’s sister,

chunks.en: or his brother's wife,
chunks.st: or with his brother’s wife,

chunks.en: or his father's brother's wife,
chunks.st: or with the wife of his father’s brother,

chunks.en: or a niddah.
chunks.st: or with a menstruating woman.

chunks.en: Also a widow who marries a Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: Likewise, one is flogged in the case of a widow who married a High Priest,

chunks.en: a divorced woman or a chalutzah who marries a regular Kohen,
chunks.st: a divorcée or a ḥalutza who married an ordinary priest,

chunks.en: a mamzeres or a nesinah who marries a regular Jew,
chunks.st: a mamzeret, i.e., a daughter born from an incestuous or adulterous relationship, or a Gibeonite woman who married a Jew of unflawed lineage,

words.note: A girl born from a forbidden relationship.
From the Givonim, who may not marry into the Jewish people.

chunks.en: or a Jewish girl who marries a nasin or a mamzer.
chunks.st: and a Jewish woman of unflawed lineage who married a Gibeonite or a mamzer,
chunks.stMore: i.e., a son born from an incestuous or adulterous relationship. The mishna elaborates:

chunks.en: If she is a widow and also divorced,
chunks.st: If a woman was both a widow and a divorcée,
chunks.stMore: as after she was widowed she remarried and was divorced,

chunks.en: a Kohen Gadol who marries her gets lashes for two different aveiros.
chunks.st: a High Priest is liable to receive two sets of lashes for marrying her due to the violation of two different prohibitions,
chunks.stMore: that of his marrying a widow and that of his marrying a divorced woman.

chunks.en: If she is divorced and also a chalutzah,
chunks.st: If a woman was both a divorcée and a ḥalutza,
chunks.stMore: from two different men,

chunks.he: אֵינוֹ חַיָּב אֶלָּא מִשֵּׁם אֶחָד בִּלְבָד:
chunks.en: a regular Kohen who marries her is punished for only one aveirah.
chunks.st: an ordinary priest who marries her is liable to receive only one set of lashes, due to the violation of one prohibition alone.

summary: More people who get lashes: for eating holy food while tamei, eating forbidden foods like cheilev, blood, chametz on Pesach, and untithed food, and for doing other aveiros. Rabbi Shimon and the Sages argue how much tevel one must eat to get lashes.
stIntro: The mishna continues enumerating those liable to receive lashes:

chunks.en: A tamei person who ate holy food from a korban,
chunks.st: A ritually impure person who ate sacrificial food

chunks.en: and one who came into the Beis HaMikdash while tamei,
chunks.st: and one who entered the Temple while ritually impure.

chunks.en: and one who eats cheilev,
chunks.st: And one who eats the forbidden fat of a domesticated animal;

words.note: Fat of an animal that the Torah forbids.

chunks.en: or blood, or nossar,
chunks.st: or blood; or notar,
chunks.stMore: leftover flesh from an offering after the time allotted for its consumption;

words.note: Meat of a korban left over after its time.

chunks.en: or piggul,
chunks.explain: A korban ruined by a wrong plan while bringing it.
chunks.st: or piggul,
chunks.stMore: an offering invalidated due to intent to sprinkle its blood, burn its fats on the altar, or consume it, beyond its designated time;

chunks.en: or a korban that became tamei,
chunks.st: or one who partakes of an offering that became impure, is flogged.

chunks.en: one who shechts or brings a korban outside the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: And one who slaughters a sacrificial animal or sacrifices it on an altar outside the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: and one who eats chametz on Pesach,
chunks.st: and one who eats leavened bread on Passover,

chunks.en: and one who eats or does melachah on Yom Kippur,
chunks.st: and one who eats on Yom Kippur and one who performs labor on Yom Kippur,

chunks.en: and one who mixes the special anointing oil for himself,
chunks.st: and one who blends the anointing oil for non-sacred use,

chunks.en: and one who mixes the ketores for himself,
chunks.st: and one who blends the incense that was burned on the altar in the Sanctuary for non-sacred use,

words.note: The special incense burned in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: and one who smears himself with the anointing oil,
chunks.st: and one who applies the anointing oil,

chunks.en: and one who eats neveilos and treifos,
chunks.st: and one who eats unslaughtered animal or bird carcasses, or tereifot,
chunks.stMore: which are animals or birds with a condition that will lead to their death within twelve months,

words.note: Animals with a deadly injury or sickness.

chunks.en: or creepy crawly creatures.
chunks.st: or repugnant creatures, or creeping animals,
chunks.stMore: is liable to receive lashes.

chunks.en: If he ate tevel, or ma'aser rishon
chunks.st: If one ate untithed produce,
chunks.stMore: i.e., produce from which terumot and tithes were not separated;

words.note: Food that terumah and ma'aser were not yet taken from.
The first tithe, given to a Levi.

chunks.en: whose terumah was not taken from it,
chunks.st: or first-tithe produce whose teruma of the tithe was not taken;

chunks.en: or ma'aser sheni or hekdesh that was not redeemed,
chunks.st: or second-tithe produce or sacrificial food that was not redeemed;
chunks.stMore: he is liable to receive lashes. With regard to the measure for liability for eating forbidden food, the mishna asks:

words.note: The second tithe, eaten in Yerushalayim.
Something given to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.he: כַּמָּה יֹאכַל מִן הַטֶּבֶל וִיהֵא חַיָּב,
chunks.en: How much tevel must one eat to get lashes?
chunks.st: How much does one need to eat from untithed produce and be liable to receive lashes?

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says, any amount.
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says: If one ate any amount
chunks.stMore: of untithed produce he is liable to receive lashes.

chunks.en: But the Sages say, a kezayis.
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say: He is liable only if he eats an olive-bulk,
chunks.stMore: which is the minimum measure characterized as eating.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon said to them,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon said to them:

chunks.en: Don't you agree with me that
chunks.st: Do you not concede to me

chunks.en: one who eats an ant of any size is punished?
chunks.st: with regard to one who eats an ant of any size that he is liable to receive lashes?

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to Rabbi Shimon:

chunks.en: That is because it is a whole creature, the way Hashem made it.
chunks.st: He receives lashes for eating an ant of any size due to the fact that it is an intact entity in the form of its creation,
chunks.stMore: and that is what the Torah prohibited.

chunks.en: He said to them,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon said to them:

chunks.en: One kernel of wheat is also whole, the way Hashem made it!
chunks.st: One kernel of wheat is also in the form of its creation, and therefore one should be liable to receive lashes for eating any intact entity.

summary: More people who get forty lashes: eating holy food at the wrong time or in the wrong place, and breaking a bone of the korban Pesach.

chunks.he: הָאוֹכֵל בִּכּוּרִים עַד שֶׁלֹּא קָרָא עֲלֵיהֶן,
chunks.en: One who eats bikkurim before the owner said the special words over them,
chunks.explain: Bikkurim are the first fruits brought to the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: In the case of a priest who eats first fruits before the one who brought the fruits to the Temple recited over those fruits the Torah verses that he is obligated to recite (see Deuteronomy 26:3–10);

chunks.en: or the holiest korbanos outside the curtains of the courtyard,
chunks.st: and one who ate offerings of the most sacred order outside the curtains surrounding the Tabernacle courtyard, or outside the Temple courtyard;

chunks.he: קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי חוּץ לַחוֹמָה,
chunks.en: or less-holy korbanos or ma'aser sheni outside the wall of Yerushalayim,
chunks.st: and one who ate offerings of lesser sanctity or second-tithe produce outside the wall of Jerusalem;

chunks.en: or one who breaks a bone of a tahor korban Pesach,
chunks.st: and also one who breaks the bone of a ritually pure Paschal offering;

chunks.en: gets forty lashes.
chunks.st: in all these cases he is flogged with forty lashes.

chunks.en: But one who leaves over meat of a tahor Pesach, or breaks a bone of a tamei one,
chunks.st: But one who leaves the flesh of the ritually pure Paschal offering until the morning of the fifteenth of Nisan, and one who breaks a bone of a ritually impure Paschal offering,

chunks.en: does not get forty lashes.
chunks.st: is not flogged with forty lashes.

summary: Someone who takes a mother bird together with her babies: Rabbi Yehuda says he gets lashes. The Sages say he sends away the mother and does not get lashes, because the aveirah can be fixed by doing a mitzvah.

chunks.en: One who takes a mother bird with her babies,
chunks.st: With regard to one who takes the mother bird with her fledglings,
chunks.stMore: thereby violating the Torah prohibition: “You shall not take the mother with her fledglings; you shall send the mother, and the fledglings you may take for yourself” (Deuteronomy 22:6–7),

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: He gets lashes and does not send away the mother.
chunks.st: He is flogged for taking the mother bird, and does not send the mother,

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: and the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: He sends away the mother and does not get lashes.
chunks.st: He sends the mother and is not flogged,

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: as this is the principle:

chunks.en: Any "do not" mitzvah
chunks.st: With regard to any prohibition

chunks.en: that has a mitzvah to get up and do something to fix it,
chunks.st: that entails a command to arise and perform a mitzva,

chunks.en: one does not get lashes for it.
chunks.st: he is not liable to receive lashes for its violation.

summary: More people who get lashes: one who makes a bald spot, shaves the corners of his head or beard, or makes a cut on his skin for someone who died. Each one counts separately.

chunks.en: One who makes a bald spot on his head,
chunks.explain: As a sign of sadness for someone who passed away.
chunks.st: One who creates a bald spot upon his head,

chunks.en: and one who shaves around the corner of his head,
chunks.st: and one who rounds the edge of his head
chunks.stMore: by shaving the hair adjacent to the ear,

chunks.en: and one who ruins the corner of his beard,
chunks.st: and one who mars the edge of his beard,

chunks.en: and one who makes one cut on his skin for someone who died,
chunks.st: and one who cuts one incision in a display of mourning over the dead,

chunks.en: gets lashes.
chunks.st: are all liable to receive lashes.

chunks.he: שָׂרַט שְׂרִיטָה אַחַת עַל חֲמִשָּׁה מֵתִים
chunks.en: If he made one cut for five people who died,
chunks.st: If he cut one incision over five dead people,

chunks.he: אוֹ חָמֵשׁ שְׂרִיטוֹת עַל מֵת אֶחָד,
chunks.en: or five cuts for one person,
chunks.st: or five incisions over one dead person,

chunks.en: he is punished for each and every one.
chunks.st: he is liable to receive lashes for each and every one.

chunks.en: For the head,
chunks.st: For rounding the edges of his head,

chunks.en: there are two corners: one on this side and one on that side.
chunks.st: one is liable to receive two sets of lashes, one from here, the hair adjacent to one ear, and one from there, the hair adjacent to the other ear.

chunks.en: For the beard,
chunks.st: For marring the edges of his beard

chunks.he: שְׁתַּיִם מִכָּאן וּשְׁתַּיִם מִכָּאן וְאַחַת מִלְּמָטָּה.
chunks.en: there are two on this side, two on that side, and one below.
chunks.st: there are two edges from here, on one side of his face, and two from there, on the other side, and one from below, on his chin.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: If he took it all off at once,
chunks.st: If he removed the hair on all the edges of his beard in one action,

chunks.en: he is punished only once.
chunks.st: he is liable to receive only one set of lashes for all of them.

chunks.en: And he is punished only if he takes it off with a razor.
chunks.st: And one is liable for marring the edges of his beard only if he removes the hair with a razor.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.he: אֲפִלּוּ לִקְּטוֹ בְמַלְקֵט אוֹ בִרְהִיטְנִי, חַיָּב:
chunks.en: Even if he pulled it out with tweezers or a scraper, he is punished.
chunks.st: Even if he removed the hair with tweezers [malket] or with a plane [rehitni], he is liable to receive lashes.

summary: One who makes a tattoo gets lashes, but only if he both scratches the skin and puts in ink. Rabbi Shimon says only if he writes a name there.

chunks.en: One who writes a tattoo,
chunks.st: One who imprints a tattoo, by inserting a dye into recesses carved in the skin, is also liable to receive lashes.

chunks.en: if he wrote with ink but did not scratch the skin,
chunks.st: If one imprinted on the skin with a dye but did not carve the skin,

chunks.en: or he scratched the skin but did not put in ink,
chunks.st: or if one carved the skin but did not imprint the tattoo by adding a dye,

chunks.en: he is not punished,
chunks.st: he is not liable;

chunks.en: until he writes and scratches, with ink or with kochol,
chunks.st: he is not liable until he imprints and carves the skin, with ink, or with kohl [keḥol],

words.note: A dark paint for the eyes.

chunks.en: or with anything that leaves a mark.
chunks.st: or with any substance that marks.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda

chunks.en: says in the name of Rabbi Shimon,
chunks.st: says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:

chunks.he: אֵינוֹ חַיָּב עַד שֶׁיִּכְתּוֹב שָׁם הַשֵּׁם,
chunks.en: He is punished only if he writes the name of an idol there,
chunks.st: He is liable only if he writes the name there,
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura explains that it means the name of an idol.

chunks.en: as it says, "Do not put a tattoo
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And a tattoo inscription

chunks.en: on yourselves; I am Hashem."
chunks.st: you shall not place upon you, I am the Lord” (Leviticus 19:28).

summary: A nazir who drinks wine all day gets only one set of lashes. But if people keep warning him and he keeps drinking, he is punished for each time.

chunks.he: נָזִיר שֶׁהָיָה שׁוֹתֶה בַיַּיִן כָּל הַיּוֹם,
chunks.en: A nazir who was drinking wine all day
chunks.st: A nazirite who was drinking wine all day

words.note: Someone who promised not to drink wine, cut his hair, or become tamei from the dead.

chunks.en: is punished only once.
chunks.st: is liable to receive only one set of lashes.

chunks.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ אַל תִּשְׁתֶּה אַל תִּשְׁתֶּה
chunks.en: If they said to him, "Don't drink! Don't drink!"
chunks.st: If onlookers said to him: Do not drink, do not drink,

chunks.en: and he keeps drinking,
chunks.st: forewarning him several times, and he drinks after each forewarning,

chunks.en: he is punished for each and every time.
chunks.st: he is liable to receive lashes for each and every drink.

summary: The same is true for a nazir who becomes tamei from the dead or shaves, and for anyone who wears sha'atnez: if they keep warning him and he keeps doing it, he is punished for each time.

chunks.en: If a nazir kept becoming tamei from the dead all day,
chunks.st: If the nazirite was rendering himself impure through exposure to corpses all day,

chunks.en: he is punished only once.
chunks.st: he is liable to receive only one set of lashes.

chunks.en: If they said to him, "Don't become tamei!
chunks.st: If they said to him: Do not render yourself impure,

chunks.en: Don't become tamei!"
chunks.st: do not render yourself impure,

chunks.en: and he kept becoming tamei,
chunks.st: and he renders himself impure after each forewarning,

chunks.en: he is punished for each and every time.
chunks.st: he is liable for each and every incident.

chunks.en: If he was shaving all day,
chunks.st: If the nazirite was shaving his hair all day,

chunks.en: he is punished only once.
chunks.st: he is liable to receive only one set of lashes.

chunks.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ אַל תְּגַלֵּחַ אַל תְּגַלֵּחַ
chunks.en: If they said to him, "Don't shave! Don't shave!"
chunks.st: If they said to him: Do not shave, do not shave,

chunks.en: and he keeps shaving,
chunks.st: and after each forewarning he shaves,

chunks.en: he is punished for each and every time.
chunks.st: he is liable for each and every time he shaves.

chunks.en: If someone was wearing sha'atnez all day,
chunks.explain: Sha'atnez is cloth of wool and linen mixed together.
chunks.st: If a person was wearing a garment consisting of diverse kinds of wool and linen all day,

chunks.en: he is punished only once.
chunks.st: he is liable to receive only one set of lashes.

chunks.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ אַל תִּלְבָּשׁ אַל תִּלְבָּשׁ
chunks.en: If they said to him, "Don't wear it! Don't wear it!"
chunks.st: If they said to him: Do not wear it, do not wear it,

chunks.en: and he takes it off and puts it on again,
chunks.st: and he removes it and dons it after each forewarning,

chunks.en: he is punished for each and every time.
chunks.st: he is liable for each and every time that he dons the garment.

summary: With one furrow of plowing, a person can break eight "do not" mitzvos at once! The mishnah lists them, and Chananya ben Chachinai adds wearing sha'atnez.
stIntro: Apropos the case where one receives several sets of lashes for performing a single action, the mishna continues:

chunks.en: There is someone who plows one furrow
chunks.st: There is one who plows a single furrow

chunks.en: and is punished for eight "do not" mitzvos:
chunks.st: and is liable to receive lashes for violating eight prohibitions.
chunks.stMore: How so?

chunks.en: one who plows with an ox and a donkey together,
chunks.st: For plowing with an ox and a donkey, in violation of the prohibition: “You shall not plow with an ox and a donkey together” (Deuteronomy 22:10);

chunks.en: and they belong to the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: and they are consecrated, and therefore he is guilty of misuse of consecrated property;

chunks.en: planting kilayim in a vineyard,
chunks.explain: Kilayim means mixing seeds of different kinds.
chunks.st: and he is plowing diverse kinds in a vineyard;

chunks.en: in the Shemittah year, on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: and it is during the Sabbatical Year, when it is prohibited to work the land; and it is on a Festival, when plowing is a prohibited labor;

chunks.en: and he is a Kohen and a nazir in a place that is tamei from the dead.
chunks.st: and he is both a priest and a nazirite and is performing the plowing in a place of impurity imparted by a corpse, which is prohibited for both a priest (see Leviticus 21:1) and a nazirite (see Numbers 6:6).

chunks.en: Chananya ben Chachinai says,
chunks.st: Ḥananya ben Ḥakhinai says:

chunks.en: Also if he was wearing sha'atnez.
chunks.st: If he was wearing a garment consisting of diverse kinds of wool and linen while plowing he is also flogged for violating that prohibition.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Sages said to him:

chunks.en: That is not the same kind.
chunks.explain: It has nothing to do with plowing.
chunks.st: That is not a prohibition in the same category as the others, as it is not connected to the act of plowing.

chunks.en: He said to them,
chunks.st: Ḥananya ben Ḥakhinai said to them:

chunks.en: Being a nazir is also not the same kind!
chunks.st: According to that criterion, the fact that he is a nazirite is also not in the same category, as a nazirite and a priest are not flogged for plowing; rather, they are flogged for contracting impurity imparted by a corpse.

summary: Malkus is thirty-nine lashes, not forty, because of how the pasuk is read. Rabbi Yehuda says it is a full forty.

chunks.en: How many lashes do they give him?
chunks.st: With how many lashes does one flog a person sentenced to receive lashes?

chunks.en: Forty minus one.
chunks.st: One flogs him with forty lashes less one,

chunks.en: As it says, "by number, forty,"
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And he shall strike him before him, in accordance with his wickedness, by number. Forty he shall strike him, he shall not add” (Deuteronomy 25:2–3).
chunks.stMore: The mishna joins the end of the first verse and the beginning of the second, forming the phrase: “By number, forty,” which is interpreted as:

chunks.en: meaning a number that is close to forty.
chunks.st: A sum adjacent to forty.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: He gets a full forty.
chunks.st: He is flogged with a full forty lashes.

chunks.en: And where does he get the extra one?
chunks.st: And where is he flogged the extra lash?
chunks.stMore: As the mishna proceeds to explain, the thirty-nine lashes are divided into three and administered in three places on the body of the person being flogged; according to Rabbi Yehuda there is one lash that remains.

chunks.en: Between his shoulders.
chunks.st: That lash is administered between his shoulders.

summary: Beis Din checks how many lashes a person can safely take, always a number that splits into three. If he cannot take more, he is let go.

chunks.en: They only decide how many he can take
chunks.st: One assesses the number of lashes that the one being punished is capable of withstanding only with

chunks.en: using a number that can be split into three.
chunks.explain: Like eighteen, which is three sixes.
chunks.st: a number of lashes fit to be divided into three equal groups.
chunks.stMore: If the assessment was that he can survive twenty lashes, he is flogged with eighteen.

chunks.en: If they decided he can take forty,
chunks.st: Likewise, if doctors assessed concerning him that he is able to receive forty lashes and survive,

chunks.en: and after he got some lashes,
chunks.st: and he is then flogged some of those forty lashes,

chunks.en: they said he cannot take forty,
chunks.st: and then they assessed him again and concluded that he cannot receive forty lashes and survive,

chunks.en: he is free from the rest.
chunks.st: he is exempt from the additional lashes.

chunks.en: If they decided he can take eighteen,
chunks.st: If the doctors initially assessed concerning him that he is able to receive only eighteen lashes,

chunks.he: מִשֶּׁלָּקָה אָמְרוּ שֶׁיָּכוֹל הוּא לְקַבֵּל אַרְבָּעִים,
chunks.en: and after he got them, they said he can take forty,
chunks.st: and once he was flogged eighteen times they assessed that he is able to receive forty,

chunks.en: he is free.
chunks.st: he is exempt from receiving additional lashes.

chunks.he: עָבַר עֲבֵרָה שֶׁיֶּשׁ בָּהּ שְׁנֵי לָאוִין,
chunks.en: If he did an aveirah that breaks two "do not" mitzvos,
chunks.st: If one performed a transgression that involves two prohibitions,

chunks.en: and they made one estimate for both,
chunks.st: and they assessed concerning him a single assessment
chunks.stMore: of the number of lashes that he could withstand in punishment for both transgressions,

chunks.en: he gets those lashes and is free.

summary: This mishnah tells the size of the strap and how the lashes were given: one third in front and two thirds behind, while the person is bent over.

chunks.en: Its handle is a tefach long, and it is a tefach wide,
chunks.st: The length of its handle is one handbreadth, and the width of the straps is one handbreadth,

words.note: About the width of a hand.

chunks.en: and its end reaches the top of his belly.
chunks.st: and the strap must be long enough so that its end reaches the top of his abdomen, i.e., his navel, when he is flogged from behind.

chunks.en: He gives him one third of the lashes in front
chunks.st: And the attendant flogs him with one-third of the lashes from the front of him, on his chest,

chunks.en: and two thirds behind.
chunks.st: and two one-third portions from behind him, on his back.

chunks.en: He does not hit him while he is standing
